options.name: Progression Balancing
options.doc:
A system that can move progression earlier, to try and prevent the player from getting stuck and bored early.

A lower setting means more getting stuck. A higher setting means less getting stuck.
options.doc_html:

options.name: Accessibility
options.doc:
Set rules for reachability of your items/locations.

**Full:** ensure everything can be reached and acquired.

**Minimal:** ensure what is needed to reach your goal can be acquired.

options.name: Story Arcs
options.doc:
Which story ladders are played. With one arc, the Singles/Doubles choosers are skipped and only that arc's
checks exist.

options.name: Goal
options.doc:
island_open: win the Island Open final (of each arc played).
dream_match: win the Dream Match at Peach's Castle (of each arc played).
completionist: check every location.

options.name: Mini-Games
options.doc:
progressive: each of the 9 Mario mini-games is a progressive item; its copies open the grid cell and levels 2 and 3.
vanilla: each mini-game is one item opening its cell; levels unlock by clearing, as in the game.
excluded: every cell is open and mini-game clears are not locations.

options.name: Shot Items
options.doc:
Your shots are items: topspin, slice and the flat shot (the second copy of each adds its power shot, or the
smash), the lob and drop shot, and the topspin, slice and flat serves (the second copy adds the nice serve).
You start with one random stroke and one random serve; a locked shot plays the first stroke or serve you own.

options.name: Story Match Sets
options.doc: Sets in every story match (best of). Vanilla keeps each match's own length.

options.name: Story Match Games
options.doc: Games per set in every story match. Vanilla keeps each match's own length.

options.name: Court Shuffle
options.doc:
The courts story matches are played on.
Shuffled: the story matches' own courts are shuffled between them, so each court is played as often as usual,
by different matches.
Randomized: every match picks its own court from the nine exhibition courts and Center Court.

options.name: Opponent Strategy
options.doc:
Where singles story opponents stand and move: every one is adaptive in the vanilla game.
Randomized: each singles match's opponent gets one of the game's eight positioning strategies, such as staying
on the baseline, sliding sideways or rushing the net. Their skill is unchanged. Doubles opponents always keep
their vanilla positioning.

options.name: Nerf Swing Contest
options.doc: Lowers the swing contest's thresholds from 100 and 150 swings to 60 and 90.

options.name: Nerf Two-on-One
options.doc: Bowser's mini-game, Two-on-One, plays 2 games per set instead of 6.
options.doc_fr: Le mini-jeu de Bowser, Two-on-One, joue 2 jeux par jeu au lieu de 6.

options.name: Experience Modifier
options.doc:
Multiplies every EXP award: story, exhibition and linked matches, drills, and EXP Bundles. A single award is
capped at 65535 and never drops to 0.

options.name: Dream Match Difficulty
options.doc:
How hard Mario plays in Peach's first Dream Match offer (Intense in the original game). After a win she lets
you pick any of the three, as usual.

options.name: Skip Intro
options.doc: A new story game skips the opening tour and starts in the Dorm Room.
options.doc_fr: Un nouveau jeu d'histoire saute la tournée d'ouverture et commence dans la salle de dortoir.

options.name: Skip Awards Ceremony
options.doc:
Winning an Island Open final goes straight from the bracket to the congratulations artwork and credits,
skipping the fireworks and the Awards Ceremony.

options.name: Default Text Speed
options.doc: The message speed a new story file starts with. It can still be changed in the game's Options.

options.name: Default Camera Mode
options.doc:
The match camera a new story file starts with: normal, or player (the court turned so you are always on the near
side). It can still be changed from the match pause menu.

options.name: Item Messages
options.doc:
Shows a message in the overworld for each item you find, send or receive. Turned off, items still arrive as
normal, just silently.

options.name: Remote Items
options.doc:
Every item, this world's own and the starting inventory included, comes from the server. Needed for co-op or
playing one slot on two carts; nothing is granted while disconnected.

options.name: DeathLink Send
options.doc:
DeathLink: send a death when you lose a point, a game or a match (the smallest loss that counts; a lost match
point is still one death). A failed mini-game or drill counts as a lost match, and a failed drill point as a
lost point; Two-on-One is a match. Change it while playing with the client's /deathlink_send command.
options.doc_fr: DeathLink: envoyer une mort lorsque vous perdez un point, un jeu ou un match (la plus petite perte qui compte; un point de match perdu est encore une mort). Un mini-jeu ou un exercice raté compte comme un match perdu, et un point de forage raté comme un point perdu; Deux sur un est un match. Changez-le en jouant avec la commande /deathlink send du client.

options.name: DeathLink Receive
options.doc:
DeathLink: what a death from another player costs you in a match: the current point, game or match (a game in
a tiebreak takes the set with it). Any death ends a mini-game or drill as failed (a high-score run already past
its record ends as a high score); Two-on-One is a match. Outside a match, mini-game or drill, deaths are
ignored. Change it while playing with the client's /deathlink_receive command.
options.doc_fr: DeathLink: ce qu'une mort d'un autre joueur vous coûte dans un match: le point actuel, le jeu ou le match (un jeu dans un tiebreak prend le jeu avec). Toute mort met fin à un mini-jeu ou à une perceuse qui a échoué (une course à haut score ayant déjà dépassé son record se termine comme un score élevé); Deux contre un est un match. En dehors d'un match, d'un mini-jeu ou d'un exercice, les décès sont ignorés. Changez-le en jouant avec la commande /deathlink receive du client.
